name: Alena And The Heater
description: "We've tried solitary confinement, waterboarding and listening to Just In Beaver, to no avail. We need something extreme." "Little Alena got an array as a birthday present ... " The array b of length n is obtained from the array a of length n and two integers l and r ( l ≤ r ) using the following procedure: b 1 = b 2 = b 3 = b 4 = 0 . For all 5 ≤ i ≤ n : b i = 0 if a i , a i - 1 , a i - 2 , a i - 3 , a i - 4 > r and b i - 1 = b i - 2 = b i - 3 = b i - 4 = 1 b i = 1 if a i , a i - 1 , a i - 2 , a i - 3 , a i - 4 < l and b i - 1 = b i - 2 = b i - 3 = b i - 4 = 0 b i = b i - 1 otherwise You are given arrays a and b ' of the same length. Find two integers l and r ( l ≤ r ), such that applying the algorithm described above will yield an array b equal to b ' . It's guaranteed that the answer exists.
input_specification: The first line of input contains a single integer n ( 5 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) — the length of a and b ' . The second line of input contains n space separated integers a 1 , ..., a n ( - 10 9 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ) — the elements of a . The third line of input contains a string of n characters, consisting of 0 and 1 — the elements of b ' . Note that they are not separated by spaces.
output_specification: Output two integers l and r ( - 10 9 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 10 9 ), conforming to the requirements described above. If there are multiple solutions, output any of them. It's guaranteed that the answer exists.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 940D — Alena And The Heater [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
